title: UI: prefer active state over queued when colouring collapsed groups
body:
Collapsed task groups and mapped tasks took their badge / border / icon colour from the backend's `agg_state()`, which ranked queued/scheduled ahead of running/deferred. A group with one queued task and five running tasks aggregated as queued even though most of its children were actively executing.

The frontend `STATE_PRIORITY` (used by the segmented state bar) already ranks active states ahead of pending ones, and its comment says it should stay in sync with the backend `state_priority`, but the backend list still had queued/scheduled first. This PR reorders `state_priority` in `airflow-core/src/airflow/api_fastapi/common/parameters.py` to put `RUNNING`/`RESTARTING`/`DEFERRED`/`AWAITING_INPUT` ahead of `QUEUED`/`SCHEDULED`, bringing the two back in sync. Since `agg_state()` is the only consumer, `taskInstance.state` on the grid API response — and every UI surface that reads it — now reflects the most-active state.

The graph state filter (`useGraphFilteredNodes.ts`) is also updated to match against *any* contained child state for aggregates rather than only the dominant one. An operator filtering for "running" expects to find running work even when it's inside a collapsed group whose dominant state is something else; the previous filter would have hidden those nodes. Leaf tasks still match by single state.
